title: Doppler shift from a moving source

questions.answer: A change in observed frequency caused by relative motion between a wave source and an observer.
accepted_alternatives: The controlled accepted alternative in the definition registry.

marking_points.text: States that observed frequency changes.
States that the change is caused by relative motion between a wave source and an observer.

questions.answer: C, it becomes four times as large.

option_feedback.B: This treats intensity as directly proportional to amplitude.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, so the factor is 2²=4.

marking_points.text: Selects C: the intensity becomes four times as large.

questions.answer: A, smaller wavefront spacing and higher observed frequency.

option_feedback.A: Correct. The approaching source compresses wavefront spacing ahead, increasing arrivals per second.
option_feedback.B: Smaller spacing gives more arrivals per second, not fewer.
option_feedback.C: Approach makes the spacing ahead smaller, not larger.
option_feedback.D: Source motion changes spacing and observed frequency.

marking_points.text: Selects A: smaller wavefront spacing and higher observed frequency.

questions.answer: C, the speed of sound through the air.

option_feedback.A: The wavelength behind a receding source is increased.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Wave speed is fixed by the unchanged stationary medium.
option_feedback.D: Wider spacing means fewer wavefronts arrive each second.

marking_points.text: Selects C: the speed of sound through the air remains unchanged.

parts.answer: The cyclist moves towards each newly emitted wavefront, so successive wavefronts ahead are closer together. They reach the stationary person more often, giving a higher observed frequency.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent causal explanation using reduced wavelength and increased arrival rate.

marking_points.text: States that successive wavefronts ahead of the approaching source are closer together.
States that more wavefronts reach the stationary person each second.
Concludes that the observed frequency is higher.

parts.answer: After passing, the cyclist is receding, so successive wavefronts reaching the person are farther apart. Fewer reach the person each second, so the observed frequency is lower.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent explanation using increased wavelength and lower arrival rate.

marking_points.text: States that wavefronts reaching the person are farther apart and arrive less often during recession.
Concludes that the observed frequency is lower.

parts.answer: Four circular wavefronts centred on S1, S2, S3 and S4, with radii increasing for earlier emissions. The fronts are crowded on the right and spread on the left.
accepted_alternatives: Correct arcs rather than complete circles.

marking_points.text: Draws successive wavefronts centred on the four emission positions, with earlier fronts having larger radii.
Shows wavefronts closer together ahead on the right and farther apart behind on the left.

parts.answer: The spacing reaching P is smaller than the spacing reaching Q because P is ahead of the moving source and Q is behind it.

marking_points.text: States that wavefront spacing at P is smaller than at Q.
Links the comparison to P being ahead of and Q being behind the right-moving source.

parts.answer: P detects a higher frequency than Q because the closer wavefronts at P arrive more often than the wider-spaced wavefronts at Q.

marking_points.text: States that P detects a higher frequency than Q.
Explains the comparison using the greater wavefront arrival rate at P.
Uses f=v/λ with 330 m s⁻¹ and 0.60 m.
Obtains 550 Hz.
Uses f=v/λ with 330 m s⁻¹ and 0.75 m.
Obtains 440 Hz.

parts.answer: Source motion makes the wavefront spacing smaller ahead and larger behind. At the same sound speed, smaller spacing gives 550 Hz while larger spacing gives 440 Hz. Thus the arrival rate and observed frequency change even though each wavefront travels at 330 m s⁻¹.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent explanation using v=fλ and the two calculated frequencies.
parts.unit_policy: Quote Hz and m s⁻¹ when numerical values are used.

marking_points.text: States that source motion changes wavefront spacing, making it smaller ahead and larger behind.
Uses the calculated 550 Hz and 440 Hz values, or their comparison, to link spacing to arrival frequency.
States that the sound speed through the unchanged air remains 330 m s⁻¹.
